newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novogen wins U.S. drug patent.
newsitem.headline: Novogen wins U.S. drug patent.

text.p: Australian drug developer Novogen Ltd said on Tuesday it had been granted patents in the United States which it says will help it become a world leader in the development of phytoetsrogen products.

Novogen said phytoestrogens, including its main product Promensil, helped address estrogen imbalances in menopausal and pre-menstrual women and were "natural anti-cancer agents" against prostate cancer in men and breast cancer in women.
The company, formerly known as Norvet, was also working on other products aimed at lowering cholesterol for women and men and treating the early stages of prostate cancer.

"With this patent position in the world's largest market, Novogen is positioned now as the world leader in the development of these human therapeutics," Novogen chairman Graham Kelly said in a statement.
Novogen managing director Chris Naughton said Promensil would be marketed in the United States as a natural source of estrogens which are gentler on humans than synthetic drugs.
The United States is the world's leading pharmaceutical market with about 50 percent of sales in therapeutic drugs.
Novogen estimated the value of the total U.S. market for the treatment of estrogen imbalances, prostate cancer and cholesterol at US$6 billion a year.
Applications for similar patents in other major countries have also been lodged.
Shares in Novogen were up 30 cents at A$1.50 by 11.55 a.m. (0155 GMT) on volume 210,911.
